result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.triads_by_type()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Group the triads of a directed graph by MAN type. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27588-L27646){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.triads_by_type() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Triads by type](/assets/graphs/triads-by-type.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a directed graph with the cycle A to B to C to A and the extra arc C to D. Right: one miniature per triad, its three nodes and arcs in the accent color, labeled with the type it is grouped under: A, B, C is the cycle 030C; A, B, D is 012; A, C, D is 021D (C points at both others); B, C, D is 021C, a two-step chain." width="100%"} Where `triadic_census()` only counts each of the 16 triad types, this method lists which triples of nodes form each type, so you can inspect, say, every 3-cycle (`"030C"`) or every transitive triple (`"030T"`) in a network of directed ties. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : MAN code to the list of node ID triples of that type (types that do not occur are left out). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Every triple is classified with `triad_type()`, $O(n^3)$; the counts agree with `triadic_census()`. Matches NetworkX's `triads_by_type` (which stores subgraphs). ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#3e23e386 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")]) {code: [[g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in t] for t in triples] for code, triples in g.triads_by_type().items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'030C': [['A', 'B', 'C']], '012': [['A', 'B', 'D']], '021D': [['A', 'C', 'D']], '021C': [['B', 'C', 'D']]} ``` ::: :::
